title: Chapter Three — A Quiet Hour Before Sunrise
excerpt: The kettle finally settled, and the words came in the order they had been waiting for. She set the page down once, twice — then trusted the line and let it stand.

title: Chapter Two — The Second Room
excerpt: Two doorways, one slightly ajar; the difference between intention and motion measured in the breadth of a finger.

title: Chapter One — Leaving the Station
excerpt: A name spoken twice in two languages — and then, on the platform, just the wind. We had agreed not to look back; one of us forgot.

title: On letting drafts breathe
excerpt: A second pass tomorrow always reads better than a first pass tonight. Park the rough cut in the deep-work folder and revisit before the morning standup.

title: Cut the windup
excerpt: Almost every paragraph I draft starts with a sentence that I should delete. The actual idea begins one breath later — usually two.
